SCP.note: Global scope and project-profile selection stay in the compact core and project facts.

AUT.note: Clarification, approval, autonomy, escalation, progress, and delegation are always-active behavior.

REQ.note: The core handles ambiguity and acceptance; project instructions hold durable local facts.

ARC.note: Architecture defaults apply in the core, with new-project detail loaded conditionally.

CODE.note: Code-quality boundaries are always active without a generic style skill.

TEST.note: TDD and evidence rules are universal; specialized test isolation stays conditional.

GIT.note: Git is a completion boundary and is evaluated as core behavior.

CICD.note: Pipeline construction and release execution use separate narrow skills.

SEC.note: Universal secret and data boundaries remain active; high-risk work loads detailed skills.

PERF.note: Performance is relevance-driven. Add a dedicated skill only after a demonstrated recurring failure.

DATA.note: Schema, integrity, lifecycle, and sensitive-data concerns are divided by task boundary.

REL.note: Reliability is designed at project setup and exercised during infrastructure and release work.

OBS.note: The observability skill carries the approved detailed defaults and verification.

UX.note: Task efficiency and accessibility load for interactive products; project facts define platforms.

DOC.note: The core requires maintained knowledge while templates keep local instructions concise.

DONE.note: Completion evidence is core behavior and installed state is independently diagnosable.

FRAME.note: Versioning, evaluations, provenance, and anti-bloat rules govern framework evolution.
